fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the access drive entrance clearly so responders can identify it quickly under low-visibility or nighttime conditions.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles and equipment to allow fire apparatus and emergency vehicles to reach all structures.
• Identify and designate a turning area near the end of the access drive so apparatus can turn around without backing a long distance on a single-lane drive.
• Keep the turning area free of stored equipment, vehicles, and other obstructions at all times.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain clearance wide enough for emergency vehicles to pass without stopping.
• Trim tree branches overhanging the access drive to maintain vertical clearance for tall apparatus such as fire engines and ambulances.
• Cut back dense vegetation between the main residence and detached structures so responders can move between buildings on foot without obstruction.
• Keep a clear path between all structures so responders can reach each building directly from the access drive.
• Post a simple site map at the driveway entrance showing the location of all structures, the parking areas, and the equipment storage area.
• Keep the equipment storage area clear of the access drive so stored items do not block vehicle movement or foot access to any structure.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove woody debris visible near structures before dry season when it can easily ignite.
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly next to the house to create open space between the plants and the walls.
• Thin trees in the cluster nearest to the structure to reduce the amount of connected vegetation that could carry fire toward the house.
• Cut back grass immediately surrounding the structure and any outbuildings to a short, mowed height.
• Separate scattered shrubs from nearby trees so fire cannot move easily from low plants up into tree branches.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation so emergency vehicles can move through without obstruction.
• Remove any dead or dry grass, leaves, and loose plant material that has collected against the base of the structure.
• Maintain the open terrain areas between scattered trees and the structure by keeping grass in those zones mowed short.
• Clear woody debris from both sides of the driveway to keep the access route open and visible.
• Thin the mixed vegetation closest to the structure to widen the open space between the plants and the building.
